messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service: redis-acceptqueue-high at 2026-03-15T07:12:09Z — PagerDuty incident PDX-5823
pagerduty: page triggered: PDX-5823 -> urgent
alice: ack'd. I'm oncall.
matt: i'm available to help, jumping in.
sana: +1 monitoring graphs now: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/redis-acceptqueue
alice: seeing accept_queue depth spike on redis-cluster-a, peer times out, pgbouncer waiting_clients up
kevin: hitting pgbouncer max_client logs: `ERROR: FATAL: remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections`
alice: ok mitigation path: 1) enable temporary client throttling rule, 2) increase pgbouncer max_client for pool, 3) failover read-only heavy tenants to read-replica route
matt: how do we add client throttle quickly? ops-bot has a simple rule toggle
ops-bot: running command: `ops throttle enable --scope=ingress --rule=non-critical` -> success
sana: after throttle, 503s drop a bit. tenant-specific spike persists for tenant `acme-inc`.
alice: running `kubectl -n infra exec pgbouncer-0 -- psql -c "show max_client_conn;"` -> returns 100
kevin: increasing to 200 on pgbouncer via configmap patch, then rolling restart. patch command:
```
kubectl -n infra patch configmap pgbouncer-config -p '{"data":{"max_client_conn":"200"}}'
kubectl -n infra rollout restart statefulset/pgbouncer
```
matt: rolling restart started, will take ~30s per pod
sana: while restart is rolling, redis accept_queue still high. looks like Redis A is overloaded; memory evictions increased
alice: can we bump redis replicas? cluster is StatefulSet managed, but we can temporarily scale read-replicas for read-heavy tenants
kevin: scaled `redis-read` sts to 3 -> command `kubectl -n data scale sts redis-read --replicas=3` -> done
sana: metrics: accept_queue depth dropped 60% after read replicas scaled and throttle
alice: customer impact: approx 1.8% 503 rate for API, mostly for acme-inc and beta testers; no data loss
matt: notify support to post status update? product wants short note
alice: @sana can you draft a brief status? include estimated recovery and mitigation steps
sana: draft: "We are investigating intermittent errors affecting some customers. We have applied traffic throttling and increased DB connection capacity; requests are recovering. No data loss suspected. We will follow up with a full incident report." -> posted to status page
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PDX-5823 acknowledged by alice
pagerduty: escalation scheduled if not resolved in 15m
alice: monitoring for next 20m, if qps normal I'll hand back
kevin: pgbouncer pods back up, no further FATAL in logs
sana: graphs stable for 10m, 503 rate down to 0.2%
alice: looks good — starting mitigation handback. final actions: leave client throttle on for 1h, keep read-replica scale at 3, schedule config PR to increase permanent pgbouncer limit and add autoscale to redis-read
matt: I'll own the PR
alice: closing incident on pagerduty
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PDX-5823 resolved by alice at 2026-03-15T07:32:00Z :white_check_mark:
alice: handing back to oncall rotation, filing post-incident notes + owners for follow-ups
sana: followups: add test that simulates accept_queue backpressure; alert tuning; runbook tweak for throttles
kevin: added TODOs on the runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/DB-AcceptQueue-Runbook
alice: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
